newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian parliament adjourns briefly over Gujarat.
newsitem.headline: Indian parliament adjourns briefly over Gujarat.

text.p: Both houses of India's parliament were adjourned till 1400 hours (0830 GMT) on Tuesday following noisy protests by members of the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) against political developments in Gujarat state.

News agencies said earlier that the deputy speaker of the Gujarat assembly, Chandu Bhai Dhabi, on Tuesday recognised as a separate group the Maha Gujarat Janata party (MGJP), a break away faction of the BJP. He had adjourned the assembly without taking up a scheduled vote of confidence.
In New Delhi, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was expected to discuss the 1996/97 (April-March) budget in an address to the lower house of parliament on Tuesday afternoon.
A ministry official said Chidambaram would now speak after the lower house resumed its sitting after lunch.
BJP members in the Lok Sabha (lower house) and Rajya Sabha (upper house) strongly objected against the Gujarat developments. The BJP is in power in the western Indian state.
Several BJP members in both houses raised slogans and went near the presiding officer's podium protesting against the deputy speaker's decision.
As the shouting persisted the presiding officers adjourned both houses till 1400 hrs.
